description: Arranges content vertically with consistent spacing.

examples.label: Example 1
examples.code:
<tp-stack>
  <tp-box>Step 1: Write a draft.</tp-box>
  <tp-box>Step 2: Review the content.</tp-box>
  <tp-box>Step 3: Publish the document.</tp-box>
</tp-stack>

attributes.name: recursive
attributes.description: Applies the stack gap recursively to descendant siblings instead of direct children only.

attributes.name: split-after
attributes.description: One-based child index after which the stack inserts a flexible split. Absent by default: no flexible split (the splitAfter property returns null). Requires available height to separate the groups.

dependencies.name: tp-base
dependencies.summary: Shared base class for tp-* components.

userHelp.introduction: The custom `<tp-stack>` element arranges content vertically with consistent spacing.
userHelp.interactions:
#### Mouse interactions

| Control or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Reading | This component organizes or presents content. |

#### Keyboard interactions

| Key or gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Component itself | No dedicated keyboard action. |
| Embedded controls, when present | Use their normal keyboard interactions. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>?</kbd> | Open User Help for the component under the pointer, or the focused component if none is hovered. Include <kbd>Shift</kbd> if needed to type <kbd>?</kbd>. |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>?</kbd> | Choose a component from the hierarchy under the pointer, or around the focused component, then open its help. <kbd>Alt</kbd> is <kbd>Option</kbd> on macOS; include <kbd>Shift</kbd> if needed to type <kbd>?</kbd>. |
